concepts.learning_objective: Explain how European settlement in the Americas, Australia and New Zealand displaced native peoples and how colonies became states.
Distinguish the different forms of control Europeans established in South Asia, Africa and settler colonies.
Describe how native histories came to be written and how native names survive in place-names.

topics.title: The Native Peoples of North America

concepts.learning_objective: Recall when and how the earliest inhabitants reached North America and how their population grew.
Describe the economy, beliefs and customs of the native peoples of North America.

topics.title: Encounters with Europeans and Mutual Perceptions

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the nature of early trade between Europeans and natives and its effects.
Compare the different European views of native Americans, from the 'noble savage' to Jefferson.
Analyse the contrast between native gift exchange and the European idea of commodities.

topics.title: Expansion of the USA and Canada and the Loss of Native Land
topics.ncert_sections: The Native Peoples Lose their Land; The Gold Rush, and the Growth of Industries

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the USA and Canada expanded and how settlers transformed the land.
Explain how native peoples lost their land through treaties, removal and reservations.
Explain how the Gold Rush, railways and industry changed North America.

topics.title: Constitutional Rights and the Winds of Change in North America
topics.ncert_sections: Constitutional Rights; The Winds of Change

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the democratic rights and the right to property in the USA excluded natives.
Trace the reforms from the Meriam survey to Canada's Constitution Act of 1982.

topics.title: Australia: Aborigines and European Settlement
topics.ncert_sections: Australia; The Europeans Reach Australia; The Development of Australia

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the origins, diversity and beliefs of Australia's native peoples.
Explain how British penal settlement led to the displacement of the aborigines.
Describe the economic development of Australia and its policy towards non-white labour.
Explain how historians and writers challenged the silence about the aborigines.
Evaluate the legal and public steps taken to recognise native land rights and past injustice.
